description:
Easy days build the engine. Hard days test it. Don't flip the two.

Four mistakes that turn easy runs into grey-zone running, and the fix for each.

Save this for your next easy run, and follow for more training explained.

#easyrun #zone2running #runningstrides #8020running #aerobicbase
alt_texts: Slide 1/7: Your easy runs are making you slower.
Slide 2/7: Mistake 1 of 4. | You run them too fast. | Easy means conversational. If you can’t talk in full sentences, you’re not going easy. | Fix: Run 60–90 s/km slower than your 5K pace.

Slide 3/7: Mistake 2 of 4. | No real rest between hard days. | Hard sessions stacked on “easy” days that aren’t easy. The engine never rebuilds. | Fix: After every hard session, go truly easy or take the day off.
Slide 4/7: Mistake 3 of 4. | Same route, same pace, every time. | Your body adapts to routine. No new stimulus, no new fitness. | Fix: Vary the terrain. Add hills. Throw in strides.
Slide 5/7: Mistake 4 of 4. | You skip strides. | The cheapest speed work in running. 20 seconds, no track, no watch. | Fix: 4–6 × 20 s strides after one or two easy runs a week.
Slide 6/7: Easy days build the engine. Hard days test it. | Don’t flip the two.
Slide 7/7: Save this for your next easy run.
